normalized.name: builtin/single-video-source
normalized.description: Data-source node — points at ONE video file to feed the SfM+STG chain. Does NOT extract frames.
normalized.docs:
Data-source node for a **single monocular video**. Symlinks the
source file into a handle so downstream reconstruction packs can
read it without copying bytes; it does **NOT** extract frames —
frame extraction happens downstream in the SfM step
(``video-to-camera-track`` / ``video-to-colmap``), which decodes
the video into per-frame images as part of its own workspace.

- **Param:** `video_path` — absolute path to a `.mp4`/`.mov`/`.mkv`.
- **Output:** `videos_dir` containing one ``input.<ext>`` symlink.
- **Output tag:** ``video-source`` (single-clip data class).
- Runs in ~1 s; fails fast if `video_path` doesn't exist.

When to use vs ``builtin/video-array-source``:

- Single monocular video (one camera, one clip) → this pack.
- Multi-camera capture or multi-clip inputs (directory of videos,
  each clip is a different camera or take) → ``builtin/video-array-source``.

Downstream (``video-to-camera-track`` / ``video-to-colmap`` /
``builtin/frame-extraction``) accepts ``video-source`` scalars (this pack) and,
when the "并行处理数组输入" arrayed checkbox is on, the equivalent
``arrayed<video-source>`` (from ``builtin/video-array-source``). The pre-arrayed
``video-source-array`` string tag was retired in the M7 migration.

Preview: derived from the ``video-source`` tag via the gateway's
tag→viewer registry (video-grid renders one tile). See
docs/pack-spec.md § "tag-driven preview inference".

video_path.description: Absolute path to the source video file (.mp4 / .mov / .MOV).

videos_dir.description: Directory containing one symlink to the source video (input.<ext>).

normalized.name: builtin/frame-extraction
normalized.description: Extract frames from a video into a directory of ``frame_XXXXXX.png`` files. Generic utility pack — works with any downstream that consumes a ``frame_sequence`` (MegaSaM, other trackers, image-space algorithms).
normalized.docs:
Frame extractor node. Takes a video and writes ``frame_XXXXXX.png``
directly into ``<output>/`` (post flatten migration — no ``frames/``
subdir), plus an ``image``-tagged handle downstream consumers pick up
automatically.

- **Input:** ``video_dir`` from ``builtin/single-video-source`` (scalar
  ``video-source``) — or ``builtin/video-array-source`` (``arrayed<video-source>``)
  when the "并行处理数组输入" checkbox is on. Each shard sees a directory
  containing one video.
- **Output:** ``image`` — one shard's output IS the ``arrayed<image>``
  sequence (files ``frame_XXXXXX.png`` sit at the handle root, no
  ``frames/`` wrapper). Under arrayable_toggle the aggregate becomes
  ``arrayed<arrayed<image>>`` with ``dim_labels=[cam,frame]`` — outer
  = per-camera shard dir, inner = per-frame file.
- **Frame selection:** ``start_frame`` / ``end_frame`` define the
  source-index window (half-open ``[start, end)``); ``skip`` is the
  stride *within* that window; ``max_frames`` is an absolute cap on
  the output count. All four mirror the STG ``pre_no_prior`` recipe.
- **Spatial downsample:** ``max_width`` shrinks wider frames to that
  width preserving aspect ratio (never upscales). 0 = keep native.
- HDR (HLG / PQ) videos are tonemapped to sRGB automatically.
- PNG compression defaults to level 1 with the sub predictor. This changes
  file size, not decoded pixels. Decoder, encoder and filter threads are
  bounded separately; defaults target eight concurrent camera shards on
  a 16-logical-CPU node. Increase encoder threads for lower concurrency.

Ships with HoloLab (no algorithm repo required). Downstream MegaSaM
(``frames-to-camera-track``) consumes this handle directly — no
re-extraction, no video decode.

video_dir.description: Directory produced by builtin/single-video-source or (with arrayed toggle on) one element of builtin/video-array-source; the first video file inside is used.

decode_threads.description: FFmpeg input decoder threads per camera.

encode_threads.description: FFmpeg PNG frame encoder threads per camera.

png_compression.description: Lossless PNG compression level; lower is faster but larger.

png_predictor.description: Reversible PNG prediction filter; does not change pixel values.

skip.description: Extract every Nth frame within the [start, end) window.

max_width.description: Downscale to this max width in px (aspect-preserved); 0 = keep native resolution. Only ever downscales — a video narrower than this passes through untouched. Mirrors ``SpacetimeGaussians/script/pre_no_prior.py`` ``--max_width`` semantics.

start_frame.description: Source-frame index (0-based, inclusive) window start. Mirrors STG ``--startframe``. Combines with ``skip``: after seeking to ``start_frame`` we pick every ``skip``-th frame from there.

end_frame.description: Source-frame index (0-based, exclusive) window end; 0 = no end, extract to video tail. Mirrors STG ``--endframe``. Must be > ``start_frame`` when set.

frame_sequence.description: Directory containing ``frame_XXXXXX.png`` files at its root (no ``frames/`` wrapper). Consumed by ``frames-to-camera-track`` and any other algorithm that needs an ordered image sequence. Port name stays ``frame_sequence`` for wiring stability; the tag is the canonical ``image`` (alias-compatible with ``image_sequence`` / ``frame_sequence``).

normalized.name: builtin/interval-pick
normalized.description: Pick every Nth element by zero-based index along an array's outer axis.

in.description: A materialized array directory of any element type; selects the outer axis.

interval.description: Index stride, not time. 2 selects indexes 0, 2, 4, ... when start is 0.

start.description: Zero-based starting index. A start beyond the array produces an empty array.

normalized.docs: Select positions start, start+interval, ... from visible outer entries ordered by basename bytes. No timestamps, FPS, frame-name parsing or content decoding. Tags and all axis names are inherited; inner arrays are untouched. Preserves selected entry names and links to resolved source elements, like slice. Output is a real directory, not an array view. Sources must remain available. Empty input or start >= N yields an empty output. Output must be empty and must not overlap input. Uses only the Python standard library in the node host runtime.
